about.title: East Palo Alto Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: East Palo Alto recorded 3 traffic deaths among its 112 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, numbers that represent real families now facing an unimaginable loss. Corridors like University Avenue, E Bayshore Road, Bay Road, and the US-101 interchange carry heavy weekday traffic, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m., a window many local commuters know well. When a fatal crash happens, California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim; other dependents or heirs may qualify if none of those relatives survive. A civil wrongful death case is separate from any criminal charges the driver may face, and it moves on its own timeline. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect grieving families in East Palo Alto with an independent attorney from our network who can review what happened and explain the deadlines that apply, including the shorter timeframe when a government vehicle or entity is involved.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You File

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits who has standing to bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then extending to other dependents or heirs if none of those relatives exist. An independent attorney can help confirm who in your family qualifies.

items.title: The Clock Starts Running Quickly
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, but that window shrinks significantly if a government entity or vehicle was involved in the crash. Given East Palo Alto's mix of city streets and the US-101 corridor, confirming which deadline applies matters early on.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek compensation for funeral costs and lost financial support, but also for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a person provided. These non-economic losses are recognized as real harm, even though they're harder to put a number on.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children have first priority to file. If none of those relatives exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible instead. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and confirm who has standing.

items.question: Is the wrongful death case connected to any criminal charges against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, even if the driver also faces criminal charges. The two proceedings run on different timelines and have different purposes, so a criminal case ending a certain way doesn't automatically decide the civil outcome.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a road like US-101 or Bay Road in East Palo Alto?
items.answer: The specific road matters mainly for identifying who was responsible and gathering evidence, such as collision reports or witness locations near known corridors like University Avenue or Bay Road. If any part of the roadway or a government vehicle was involved, the filing deadline can be shorter, so it helps to have that reviewed early.
